Generic PEI inserts one frame-index store for every non-register callee-save before emitPrologue.  C166 walks exactly that CalleeSavedInfo list to place the DWARF state change after the last such store; a missing store would be a PEI/backend consistency bug, not a source-language condition.

paths.expression: FrameReg == C166::R0 && !Ref.getScalable() && "C166 callee save is not in the fixed user-stack frame"
paths.rationale: Ordinary C166 callee-saves are fixed frame-index objects allocated by TargetFrameLowering on the DPP1:R0 user stack.  C166 has no scalable stack objects; interrupt saves take the separate PUSH/POP path and are excluded here.

paths.expression: Offset.getValueType() == MVT::i16 && "unexpected C166 indirect-branch address type"
paths.rationale: BRIND lowering supplies either a far address whose low word is selected here or an already narrowed 16-bit code offset; no other indirect-branch pointer type is legal for C166.

paths.expression: PointerType == MVT::i16 && "unexpected C166 jump-table pointer type"
paths.rationale: Small-model jump-table symbols use a 16-bit pointer; Large and Medium select the separate 32-bit far-address path immediately above this assertion.

paths.rationale: c166_bank is a function-type attribute encoded as a dedicated far function address space.  Sema rejects combining it with the only 16-bit function-pointer form (_near), so every legal C bank switch reaches lowering with a 32-bit segment:offset callee.

paths.expression: "C166 interrupt handler cannot be called directly"
paths.rationale: Sema diagnoses every direct C call to a declaration carrying the C166 interrupt attribute.  The backend diagnostic remains a defensive check for hand-written invalid IR using the interrupt calling convention at a call site.

paths.expression: "C166 interrupt handler must have void (void) signature"
paths.rationale: The C166 interrupt attribute handler accepts only a prototyped void(void) function and issues a source diagnostic otherwise.  The backend check protects the calling-convention contract against malformed hand-written IR.
